messages.subject: Example 02 / Evaluating disease damage
parts:
Hello everybody, 
I'm new in the forum and I would like to learn to process my images with fieldImageR.
I have images of grain and I would like to calculate the following characteristics for each individual image:  
• coverage % of total crop area in the image (based on pixel)
• coverage % of damaged area in the leaves 
• arithmetic mean values for different indices based on crop coverage 
At the end I need a list with the results for each picture, preferably indices with stabw and min max values. 

Thanks to Filipe, I know what I need is described excellently on: https://phenome-force.github.io/FIELDimageR-workshop/  Example 02 / Evaluating disease damage (Tomato Breeding). Many thanks for this great work. 
Now I want to understand the workflow and adapt it to my pictures. 
Unfortunately I am not the R expert and I would be happy if you could give me some answers to my questions in your script:

# Images names (folder directory: "./EX2/")
pics<-list.files("C:/R/10xSickte9/")
pics

# Vegetation indices 
index<- c("BI","GLI","NGRDI")

#Choose one image to prepare the pipeline
EX.L1<-stack(paste("C:/R/10xSickte9/",pics[1],sep = ""))
plotRGB(EX.L1) 

# Shapefile with extent=T (The whole image area will be the shapefile)
EX.L.Shape<-fieldPolygon(mosaic=EX.L1, extent=T) 

# Select one index to identify leaves and remove the background
EX.L2<-fieldMask(mosaic=EX.L1, index="BGI", cropValue=0.8, cropAbove=T) 

plotRGB(EX.L2$newMosaic)
### for a fine adjustment of the result, I would like to display the result in original size. I would like to zoom down to the pixel level. Maybe export out of R? How can I do that?

# Select one index to identify damaged area in the leaves  
EX.L3<-fieldMask(mosaic=EX.L2$newMosaic, index="VARI", cropValue=0.1, cropAbove=T) 

plotRGB(EX.L3$newMosaic)
### same here….

# Indices
EX.L4<-fieldIndex(mosaic=EX.L2$newMosaic, index=index)

# Making a new stack raster with new layers (damage area and indices)
EX.L5<-stack(EX.L4[[index]],(1-EX.L2$mask),(1-EX.L3$mask)) 
names(EX.L5)<-c(index,"Area","Damage")
plot(EX.L5)

# projection=F (Ignore projection. Normally used only with remote sensing images)
EX.L.Info<- fieldInfo(mosaic=EX.L5, 
                      fieldShape=EX.L.Shape$fieldShape, 
                      projection=F)

# Combine information from all images in one table
EX.L.Info$plotValue 


# Necessary packages
library(foreach)
library(parallel)
library(doParallel)

# Number of cores
n.core<-3
### What exactly I can set here?

# Starting parallel
cl <- makeCluster(n.core, output = "")
registerDoParallel(cl)
system.time({
  EX.Table <- foreach(i = 1:length(pics), .packages = c("raster","FIELDimageR"), 
                      .combine = rbind) %dopar% {
                        EX.L1<-stack(paste("C:/R/10xSickte9/",pics[i],sep = ""))
                        EX.L.Shape<-fieldPolygon(mosaic=EX.L1, extent=T, plot=F)
                        EX.L2<-fieldMask(mosaic=EX.L1, index="BGI", cropValue=0.8, cropAbove=T, plot=F) 
                        EX.L3<-fieldMask(mosaic=EX.L2$newMosaic, index="VARI", cropValue=0.1, cropAbove=T, plot=F)   
                        EX.L4<-fieldIndex(mosaic=EX.L2$newMosaic, index=index, plot=F)
                        EX.L5<-stack(EX.L4[[index]],(1-EX.L2$mask),(1-EX.L3$mask)) 
                        names(EX.L5)<-c(index,"Area","Damage")
                        EX.L.Info<- fieldInfo(mosaic=EX.L5, fieldShape=EX.L.Shape$fieldShape, projection=F) 
                        EX.L.Info$plotValue 
                      }})
EX.Table.2<-data.frame(Genotype=do.call(rbind,strsplit(pics,split = ".jpeg")),EX.Table[,-1])
EX.Table.2
### how I can save the results automatically as .txt or .csv in the picture files folder?
### What exactly means  the value of BI, Area and Damage? 
  ID       BI       GLI      NGRDI      Area    Damage
1  1 86.16558 0.1277212 0.06399235 0.2581252 0.4635286

I would appreciate your support,
best regards,
Dominik

messages.author: c59b667c61f258ae
messages.subject: Re: Example 02 / Evaluating disease damage
parts:
Hi Dominik, 
Thank you for contacting. 

################ 
### Question 1 ### 
################

plotRGB(EX.L2$newMosaic) 
### for a fine adjustment of the result, I would like to display the result in original size. I would like to zoom down to the pixel level. Maybe export out of R? How can I do that?

Unfortunately, FIELDimageR does not have image zooming yet. One solution for Windows is to use the code: 

x11() 
plotRGB(EX.L2$newMosaic) 

There are many different ways to save images using R (e.g., TIFF, JPG, PDF, etc.). 
Here, there is some material from where you can read more about that:
 • https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/raster/versions/3.4-5/topics/writeRaster 
• https://www.r-bloggers.com/2013/03/high-resolution-figures-in-r/ 
• https://www.datamentor.io/r-programming/saving-plot/ 

################ 
### Question 2 ### 
################

# Number of cores n.core<-3 
### What exactly I can set here?

This is the number of cores from your computer that you want to use on the parallel step (a common computer has around 4 to 8 cores). It helps to accelerate the analysis. 

################ 
### Question 3 ### 
################

EX.Table.2 
### how I can save the results automatically as .txt or .csv in the picture files folder?

The command to save tables in R is: 

write.csv(EX.Table.2,file = "Table.csv",col.names = T, row.names = F) 

There is more information in the tutorial. Here is the link: https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#P17 

################ 
### Question 4 ### 
################

### What exactly means  the value of BI, Area and Damage? 
ID       BI       GLI      NGRDI      Area    Damage 
1  1 86.16558 0.1277212 0.06399235 0.2581252 0.4635286

BI is the Brightness Index. “BI, GLI, and NGRDI” are vegetation indices. For more information please check: https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#P6 

“Area” in this case is the whole object area in the picture identified by using the index BGI (code line EX.L2 where fieldMask was used to remove the background) 

“Damage” is the area affected by the disease according to the index VARI (code line EX.L3). Basically, I used the index VARI in the function fieldMask to diagnose disease damage. 

I recommend changing the code for your crop and disease. For instance, one suggestion is to change the Index on fieldMask to choose the one that provides better accuracy/performance. 

Hope it can help you.
All the best,
Filipe

Dear Filipe,

Thank you for your answer. It works great, I'm thrilled 😊. However there remain many questions:

To adapt my pictures, I use QGIS. Here I can calculate all the Indices and the results are wonderfully on top of each other. I can zoom into the picture and decide where the damage begins and where it ends. Unfortunately, it doesn't seem that easy to separate the damage from the soil with my RGB image. 

Question 1

I would like to delete all objects smaller than e.g. 1000 pixels, because I think in my case it will improve the accuracy of the results. How can i build this into your loop?

One last question about the results: the values of the indices are mean values of the selected leaf area, right? I would like to add the standard deviation and min / max values for each indice in my EX.Table.2. How does it work?
I am very happy to understand the workflow more and more and thanks for your help,

parts:
Hi Dominik,

Thanks for asking. I am going to try answering some of your questions. Hope someone in our community helps us too.

Question 1

My original picture is about 7MB. If I load the picture in R and immediately export it again, the picture size increases up to 46MB, during this the resolution decreases. Why the file is so inflated? Is the resolution of the original image somewhere reduced in your model, to save computing time if necessary? I really want to calculate with the original size in the entire model, is this done so fare?

I don’t know yet why it is happening. Other people already asked about that before and I don’t have a good answer yet. I do not include any code to reduce the picture resolution inside FIELDimageR functions. However, outside the functions on the pipeline code (scripts), I suggested using the aggregate function from the raster package as an alternative to accelerate the time to do the analysis. I guess the way that I suggested to save images after processing (https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#P17) maybe is causing problems with resolution. This situation didn’t happen to me yet. Let’s wait if someone here can help us to understand what’s going on.

Question 2

In my example I detect the plants with HUE and threshold value 0.5. I found more than 26000 objects smaller than 1000 pixels, that are not plants. I would like to delete all objects smaller than e.g. 1000 pixels, because I think in my case it will improve the accuracy of the results. How can i build this into your loop?

I need to check your code to see the functions that you are using. If you are counting objects with fieldCount (https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#P7) or fieldObject (https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#P11) you can use the parameter minSize = 1000 or minArea = 1000. Otherwise, you can use one of those functions to create a new mask to remove these small objects. Could you please share your code here?

Question 3

If I look at the results in EX.Table.2, I find the values ​​for BI, GLI, NGRDI. I cannot see in the loop where these three indices were defined. BLI and VARI were used for area and damage, I see them clearly. Where are the other indices hidden and how I can exchange them?

Those were identified on index object (https://github.com/OpenDroneMap/FIELDimageR#P19):

# Vegetation indices

index<- c("BGI","VARI","SCI")

 Just remember that these indices are relative measurements using the digital number from your camera. They give you an idea of relative differences among your treatments. The value per se is not biologically determined directly. They only will be related with reflectance if you make the radiation correction or luminosity correction.

Question 4

One last question about the results: the values of the indices are mean values of the selected leaf area, right? I would like to add the standard deviation and min / max values for each indice in my EX.Table.2. How does it work?

That’s a great question. I have some ideas on how to make it easier and faster, but I didn’t have time yet to implement them. But right now, one possible solution is (that’s will take more time):

 

EX.L.Info<- fieldInfo(mosaic=EX.L5, fieldShape=EX.L.Shape$fieldShape, ﻿fun = "mean", projection=F)

EX.L.Info1<- fieldInfo(mosaic=EX.L5, fieldShape= EX.L.Info$fieldShape, fun = "sd", projection=F) 

EX.L.Info2<- fieldInfo(mosaic=EX.L5, fieldShape= EX.L.Info1$fieldShape, fun = "min", projection=F)

EX.L.Info3<- fieldInfo(mosaic=EX.L5, fieldShape= EX.L.Info2$fieldShape, fun = "max", projection=F)

EX.L.Info3$plotValue

 

Let me know if it makes sense.

All the best,

Filipe

how do you export your images? Can you paste your code?
For some formats there are some option related to compression algorithms
see
?tiff
(omissis)
tiff(filename = "Rplot%03d.tif",
     width = 480, height = 480, units = "px", pointsize = 12,
     compression = c("none", "rle", "lzw", "jpeg", "zip", "lzw+p", "zip+p"),
 
?writeRaster
(omissis)
options: Character. File format specific GDAL options. E.g., when writing a geotiff file you can use: options=c("COMPRESS=NONE", "TFW=YES")

EX.Table <- foreach(i = 1:length(pics), .packages = c("raster","FIELDimageR"),
